chunks: And it is narrated from al-Faḍl ibn Abī Qurrah, who said:
We entered upon Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام while he was working in a garden belonging to him. So we said: “May Allah make us your ransom, let us work for you, or let the servants do it.”
He said: “No, leave me, for I desire that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sees me working with my own hand and seeking the halal, despite hardship to myself.”

key_terms.بِيَدِي: with my own hand, by my own direct effort
key_terms.حَائِطٍ: a garden or enclosed orchard owned by a person

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith teach about working with one’s own hands and seeking halal livelihood?
ai.summary: This hadith presents Imam Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام personally engaging in labor and seeking halal livelihood through his own effort. It highlights the virtue of dignified work, self-reliance, and willingly bearing hardship in the pursuit of lawful sustenance.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.3595 - It is narrated from Al-Fadl ibn Abi Qurrah:
"We entered upon Abu Abdullah (as) while he was working in his garden.
We said: 'May Allah (swt) make us your ransom! Let us work for you, or let the servants handle it.'
Imam (as) replied: 'No, leave me to it, for I desire that Allah (swt), the Almighty and Majestic, sees me working with my own hands and seeking lawful sustenance, even if it causes hardship to myself.'"
